newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt prices weaken on long bond sale fears.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt prices weaken on long bond sale fears.

text.p: * Indian government security prices were down in thin trade in early afternoon trade on Thursday trade, dealers said.
* Prices down in anticipation of central bank selling privately-placed bonds. Indian government placed 50 billion rupees of 10-year 13.05 percent bonds with Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday.
* "Market is nervous," said a dealer. "The 10-year bond was traded at 12.60 percent but government placed it with RBI at 13.05. If RBI puts the bond up for sale, long bond prices will really crash."
* Dealers said prices of the ten-year bond were down by 1.0 rupee and other gilt prices were also down on Thursday but volumes were poor.
* In latest deals, 13.50 percent 1998 traded at 103.75 rupees against Wednesday's 104.20, the 13.40 percent 1999 stock at 107.70 against 107.90 and 13.80 percent 2002 at 108.50 against 108.60.
* Dealers said the April 10, 1998 treasury bill was traded unchanged at a yield of 8.6 percent.
* The treasury bill auctioned on Wednesday at 9.0 percent was traded on Thursday at 8.8 percent, dealers said.
